text: Cohen suspects Anahora is the world depicted on the blasphemous banner in Lazla's church, showing a three-eyed fanged figure devouring Verkieri and their victims, and theorizes it may be the same being Leonuka bargained with.
The narrator theorizes that the gargoyles' construction, human bodies sealed in fired clay, is inspired by the concept of golems from Jewish folklore.
Isbrand believed Verkieri should remain hidden and obey ancient restrictions, while Brenis wanted to abandon restraint and openly dominate humanity.
Lakra believes Kalas was meddling with the same power that Brenis is trying to harness.
Lakra suspects Kalas's unusually deep connection to Anahora is what preserved his body in plant form.
Brenis later explains his goal was to embrace and harness the Anacorin curse carried by the Verkieri rather than resist it.
Brenis was attempting to create a controlled breach into Anahora to draw power into the material world while retaining control, but Lakra's sabotage left the breach uncontrolled.
